entries.q: How is real estate bookkeeping different from regular small business bookkeeping?
ask: what makes real estate bookkeeping different
why do I need a real estate bookkeeper
can a regular bookkeeper do my books
why do real estate investors need a specialized bookkeeper
what makes bookkeeping for investors different
a: Real estate books are set up property by property and flip by flip. Rentals need income and expenses tracked for each property, loan principal split from interest, and depreciation. Flips hold their costs on the balance sheet until the sale, then move them to cost of goods sold. A standard small business setup isn't built for either, which is why every REVI file is set up around your flips and properties.

source.label: From FAQs: How is real estate bookkeeping different from regular small business bookkeeping?

entries.q: Does a flip get depreciated?
ask: is depreciation allowed on a flip
does depreciation apply to a flip
a: No. Depreciation applies to property held to produce income. A flip is held for sale, so it doesn't depreciate. That's the reason flip books and rental books look nothing alike.

source.label: From FAQs: Does a flip get depreciated?

entries.q: Are rehab costs deductible when you pay them?
ask: can I deduct rehab right away
do I get to write off the rehab now
a: Generally no. On a property held for sale, materials, labor, permits, and carrying costs get added to the cost of the property rather than deducted as paid. They come back as cost of goods sold when it sells.

source.label: From FAQs: Are rehab costs deductible when you pay them?

entries.q: Why do flip costs sit on the balance sheet?
ask: why don't flip costs show on my p&l
why dont my flip costs show as expenses
a: Because until it sells, the property is inventory. If those costs hit the profit and loss as they happened, every month before the sale would show a loss and the closing month would show a windfall that isn't real.

source.label: From FAQs: Why do flip costs sit on the balance sheet?

entries.q: Does a 1031 exchange apply to a flip?
ask: can I do a 1031 on a flip
a: No. A 1031 applies to property held for investment or productive use. A flip is held for sale, which puts it outside the rules. 1031 exchange documentation is a landlord service.

source.label: From FAQs: Does a 1031 exchange apply to a flip?

entries.q: What's the difference between bookkeeping for a flip and bookkeeping for a rental?
ask: how are flips and rentals booked differently
a: A rental produces income every month, so its books are a profit and loss with a depreciation schedule. A flip produces nothing until it sells, so costs build up on the balance sheet and release all at once at closing. Running flips through rental-style books misstates every month in between.

source.label: From FAQs: What's the difference between bookkeeping for a flip and bookkeeping for a rental?

entries.q: Does loan principal show up on a rental's profit and loss?
a: No, only the interest. Principal reduces the loan balance on the balance sheet. Splitting the payment wrong makes a property look less profitable than it is.

source.label: From FAQs: Does loan principal show up on a rental's profit and loss?

entries.q: What's the difference between a repair and a capital improvement?
ask: is a new roof a repair
is a new hvac a repair or an improvement
is a water heater a capital improvement
a: A repair keeps the property in working condition and is deducted in the year it happens. An improvement adds value or extends useful life and gets depreciated over time.

source.label: From FAQs: What's the difference between a repair and a capital improvement?

entries.q: Do I need separate books for flips and rentals?
ask: should flips and rentals be separate
separate books for flipping and renting
do I need two sets of books
can flips and rentals share one set of books
a: Separate tracking at minimum. The two are taxed differently, and mixing them makes it harder to apply the right treatment to each. How far to take the separation, tracking versus separate entities, is a question for your CPA.

source.label: From FAQs: Do I need separate books for flips and rentals?

entries.q: Who is monthly bookkeeping built for?
ask: how many properties do I need
who is the monthly service for
a: Flippers doing 2 or more flips a year, and landlords with 2 or more rentals. At that point there are enough transactions each month that the books stop being a once-a-year cleanup and start being something worth keeping current. With a single property, a spreadsheet and a good CPA at year end usually covers it.

source.label: From FAQs: Who is monthly bookkeeping built for?

entries.q: When is the right time to bring in a bookkeeper?
ask: when should I hire a bookkeeper
is it time to get a bookkeeper
how many properties before I need a bookkeeper
how do I know it is time for a bookkeeper
a: Usually around the second or third property, or the second flip running at the same time. One property you can track by hand. What changes is the number of transactions: more accounts, more contractor payments, draws, closing statements, and a year-end pile that stops being something you can reconstruct from memory in April.

source.label: From FAQs: When is the right time to bring in a bookkeeper?

entries.q: Why hand off bookkeeping for rental properties?
ask: why hire a bookkeeper for rentals
why outsource bookkeeping for my rentals
why hire a bookkeeper for rental properties
a: Every rental adds work each month. Rent, repairs, and loan payments all need to be recorded and reconciled, with principal kept apart from interest, so you can see what each property actually makes. Kept current, the books give you NOI by property all year and a year-end package your CPA can file from.

source.label: From FAQs: Why hand off bookkeeping for rental properties?

entries.q: What's the difference between a bookkeeper and a CPA?
ask: do I still need a cpa
what is the difference between bookkeeping and accounting
what does a bookkeeper do compared to a cpa
a: Different jobs, and most investors need both. Bookkeeping is the month-to-month work, recording transactions, reconciling accounts, tracking costs by property, and producing the reports. A CPA takes those reports at year end, applies tax law, and files the return. The cleaner the books are, the less there is for the CPA to reconstruct.

source.label: From FAQs: What's the difference between a bookkeeper and a CPA?

entries.q: Who do you work with?
ask: do you work with small businesses
what kind of clients do you have
do you work outside north carolina
a: We work with house flippers and long-term rental landlords anywhere in the US, and with investors who do both. Every file we keep is a real estate file, so the books are set up around your flips and properties from the start.

entries.q: Do you work with house flippers?
ask: do you work with flip investors
a: Flips move fast, with contractor payments, draws, and closings running on several at once. We keep every cost with its flip, so you can see what each one has cost so far and what it cleared when it sold. We work best with flippers doing 2 or more flips a year, including BRRRR investors with rehab work and flippers using hard money.

entries.q: Do you work with landlords?
ask: do you work with rental property owners
a: We build your books around your properties, so you can see what each one makes every month. We work best with landlords who own 2 or more rentals, from single-family and small multifamily to buy-and-hold and BRRRR, including owners with several LLCs.

entries.q: I flip and hold rentals. Can you do both?
ask: I flip and also own rentals
a: If you flip and hold rentals, both sides live in one QuickBooks file and are kept apart, so each follows its own rules. You see what each flip cleared and what each rental made, next to the total for the whole portfolio.

entries.q: Who is Julia?
ask: who will I be working with
a: Hi, I'm Julia Kachula, the bookkeeper and founder of REVI Bookkeeping, based in Charlotte, NC. My focus is bookkeeping for flippers and long-term rental landlords, and because everything runs in the cloud, I work with investors anywhere in the US.

My background is in accounting and financial reporting. I started REVI because real estate books rarely look like a typical business's. Flips hold their costs until they sell, rentals need numbers by property, and some investors run both.

a: We do not sell the personal information of Consumers. If You have any questions about this, please contact Us at info@revibookkeeping.com.

entries.q: Is my financial information secure?
a: As part of delivering Our bookkeeping services, We may collect and process sensitive financial data, including bank statements, transaction records, payroll information, and other financial documents. This information is provided directly by You or Your authorized representative and is used solely to perform the services You have engaged Us to provide. This information is processed within QuickBooks Online and is subject to Intuit’s security and privacy practices.

The security of Your Personal Data is important to Us. We implement industry-standard technical and organizational security measures to protect Your Personal Data, including secure cloud storage through QuickBooks Online and encrypted communications. However, please be aware that no method of transmission over the Internet, or method of electronic storage, is 100% secure. While We strive to use commercially acceptable means to protect Your Personal Data, We cannot guarantee its absolute security.

entries.q: How do I delete my data?
a: You have the right to request the deletion of Your personal data that We hold. To make this request, please send an email to info@revibookkeeping.com with the subject line “Request for Data Deletion.” In Your email, provide Your name and the email address associated with Your account to help Us verify and process Your request promptly.
